section: Step 3: keep the work apart from the windows
text: Put the calculation in a module of its own, checks.py, with plain functions on the project. They need no window, so they are easy to test and to reuse in a menu command, a window and a toolbox tool alike: from dataclasses import dataclass DEFAULTS = {"min_pressure_m": 10.0, "max_pressure_m": 60.0, "min_velocity_mps": 0.3, "max_velocity_mps": 2.0, "max_headloss_m_per_km": 10.0} @dataclass class Finding: kind: str # "node" or "link" element_id: str name: str check: str value: float limit: float severity: str # "High", "Medium" or "Low" def check_design(project, limits=None): limits = {**DEFAULTS, **(limits or {})} results = project.results or {} nodes = {row["name"]: row for row in results.get("nodes", [])} found = [] for node in project.nodes: row = nodes.get(node.name) if node.node_type != "JUNCTION" or row is None: continue pressure = float(row["pressure_m"]) if pressure < limits["min_pressure_m"]: found.append(Finding("node", node.id, node.name, "Pressure below the minimum (m)", pressure, limits["min_pressure_m"], "Medium")) return found What the project holds is in The project model: project.nodes and project.links with their values, project.results after a run (one row per node and link, with pressure_m, head_m, flow_lps, velocity_mps, headloss_m), and project.link_length_m(link). The full checks.py of the example also checks velocities, head loss per kilometre and dead ends.

section: Step 4: register what the plugin adds
text: __init__.py defines register(host). FlowCHAOS calls it when the plugin is switched on and gives it the host, the main window (Plugin API): from . import checks def register(host): host.add_tool_window("design-check-report", "Design Check Report", lambda: _window(host), "Pressures, velocities and head losses outside the design limits") add_tool_window puts a command in the Plugins menu that opens your window beside the map, one at a time. add_plugin_action(text, callback, tooltip) adds a plain command instead.

section: Step 5: a window of your own
text: A window is ordinary Qt (PySide6). Build it in a function that returns it: def _window(host): from PySide6.QtWidgets import QLabel, QPushButton, QTableWidget, QTableWidgetItem, QVBoxLayout, QWidget window = QWidget() window.setWindowTitle("Design Check Report") layout = QVBoxLayout(window) summary = QLabel("Run a steady-state analysis, then Check.") table = QTableWidget(0, 4) table.setHorizontalHeaderLabels(["Severity", "Check", "Element", "Value"]) check = QPushButton("Check") layout.addWidget(summary) layout.addWidget(table, 1) layout.addWidget(check) def run_check(): found = checks.check_design(host.document.project) table.setRowCount(len(found)) for r, f in enumerate(found): for c, value in enumerate((f.severity, f.check, f.name, round(f.value, 2))): table.setItem(r, c, QTableWidgetItem(str(value))) summary.setText(f"{len(found)} finding(s).") host.canvas.set_selection({(f.kind, f.element_id) for f in found}) # shown on the map check.clicked.connect(run_check) return window host.canvas.set_selection({("node", id), ("link", id)}) selects elements on the map; the user sees them highlighted and can zoom to them with Ctrl+J.

section: Step 6: a tool in the Processing Toolbox
text: A toolbox tool declares its parameters; FlowCHAOS builds the form, the help, the log, the result table and the map selection: def _toolbox_run(project, values, context): from flowchaos.core.processing import Outcome found = checks.check_design(project, values) return Outcome(f"{len(found)} finding(s).", ["Severity", "Check", "Element"], [[f.severity, f.check, f.name] for f in found], select={(f.kind, f.element_id) for f in found}) def register(host): from flowchaos.core.processing import Algorithm, Param host.add_toolbox_algorithm(Algorithm( "design_check_report", "Design check report", "Checks", "tb-check", "Every value of the last run outside the limits.", (Param("min_pressure_m", "Minimum pressure", "number", 10.0, suffix=" m"),), _toolbox_run, needs="results")) needs keeps the tool greyed until it makes sense: network, links, selection, results or none. A tool that changes the network sets changes=True: the toolbox then runs it as one step of Undo, and new elements join the network layer being edited.

Every change goes through the document, as one step the user can undo: def set_material(project): for link in project.links: if link.link_type == "PIPE" and link.diameter_mm <= 110: link.attributes["material"] = "HDPE" host.network_edit("Set materials of small pipes", set_material) host.network_edit(label, edit) makes the change in the network layer being edited (and asks which layer when several exist); host.document.apply(label, edit) changes the project as a whole (settings, results). Never keep project.nodes or a node between two edits: each edit makes a new project, so read host.document.project again each time.

section: Step 8: long work in the background
text: A calculation that takes more than a moment must not freeze the window. Run it on a worker and hand the result back with a Qt signal: from PySide6.QtCore import QObject, Signal from flowchaos.core import workers class Done(QObject): finished = Signal(object) done = Done() done.finished.connect(show_results) # runs on the window's thread project = host.document.project # read here, then work on it there workers.submit(lambda: done.finished.emit(checks.check_design(project)), pool_name="compute") Never touch windows from the worker: compute there, show the result in the connected function.

section: Step 9: try it while you write it
text: Edit the files of the installed copy (Plugins > Manage Plugins > Open Plugin Folder), or build again with the Plugin Builder. Press Reload in Plugins > Manage Plugins: the plugin is switched off and on again, reading its files anew. No restart is needed. An error while loading is shown in the Plugin Manager (point at the plugin's name) and written to the log (Help > Open Crash Log Folder, flowchaos.log). Test the plain functions with pytest, without starting FlowCHAOS: from flowchaos.core.sample_library import town_water_supply from flowchaos.core.solver_backend import run_with_best_backend from flowchaos.ui.main_window import prepare_results import checks def test_finds_high_pressures(): project = town_water_supply() project.results, _message = prepare_results(run_with_best_backend(project)) assert any(f.check.startswith("Pressure above") for f in checks.check_design(project))

Zip the folder (the folder itself, with plugin.json inside it) and send the ZIP. Your colleagues install it with Plugins > Manage Plugins > Install from ZIP and tick it. Raise version in plugin.json for each new release; installing a newer ZIP replaces the older one.

Name things as the engineer sees them: "Design check report", not "dcr_tool". Keep the calculation in plain functions and test them; keep windows thin. Every change through network_edit or document.apply, never by changing host.document.project directly, so Undo and the map stay right. Work longer than half a second goes to a worker (Step 8). unregister(host) stops anything the plugin started itself: timers, threads, open files. What was added through the host is removed by FlowCHAOS. A plugin runs with the user's permissions: write only to files the user chooses. More examples are in Plugin examples; every call is in Plugin API.
The objects a plugin receives and the calls it can make.

register(host) receives the host: the FlowCHAOS main window. Member What it is host.document the open project and its undo history (see below) host.main_window the main window, to parent your dialogs and windows host.canvas the map host.add_plugin_action(text, callback, tooltip="") adds a command to the Plugins menu and returns its QAction host.remove_plugin_action(action) removes a command host.statusBar().showMessage(text, milliseconds) a short message in the status bar host.show_tool_window(key, factory) opens a window of yours beside the map (one per key) host.add_tool_window(key, title, factory, tooltip="") a Plugins menu command that opens your window host.add_toolbox_algorithm(algorithm) adds a tool to the Processing Toolbox (flowchaos.core.processing.Algorithm) host.remove_toolbox_algorithm(id) removes it (done for you when the plugin is switched off) host.add_rate_source(name, provider) rates for the BOQ Workbench: provider(boq) returns {description: rate} host.rate_sources the rate sources currently available

host.document holds the project and every change to it. Member What it does document.project the NetworkProject (see project model) document.apply(label, edit) runs edit(project) as one undoable step called label document.apply_field(label, name, value) sets one field of the project (for example results) undoably document.changed a signal emitted after every change document.projectReplaced a signal emitted when another project is opened document.file_path the project's file, or None before it is saved Changing the project: def double_demands(project): for node in project.nodes: if node.node_type == "JUNCTION": node.demand_lps *= 2 host.document.apply("Double the withdrawals", double_demands) The step appears in Edit > Undo as "Double the withdrawals", the project is marked unsaved and the map, tables and panels refresh.

Member What it does canvas.selection a set of ("node", id) and ("link", id) canvas.set_selection(items) selects elements canvas.zoom_to_selection() zooms to them canvas.fit_network() shows the whole network canvas.set_map_views(node_view, link_view) colours the map (keys as in flowchaos.core.map_views) canvas.refresh() redraws after you changed display settings

from flowchaos.core.solver_backend import run_with_best_backend results = run_with_best_backend(host.document.project) for node in results.nodes: # name, head_m, pressure_m, demand_lps, quality print(node.name, node.pressure_m) for link in results.links: # name, flow_lps, velocity_mps, headloss_m, quality, status print(link.name, link.flow_lps) Extended period: run_extended_with_best_backend(project, duration_seconds, timestep_seconds) returns frames, each with time_seconds and hydraulics (nodes and links as above).

from flowchaos.core.pipe_sizing import pipe_series, size_pipes, apply_sizes from flowchaos.core.fire_flow import fire_flow_analysis, hydrant_candidates project = host.document.project pipes = [l.id for l in project.links if l.link_type == "PIPE"] sizing = size_pipes(project, pipes, pipe_series()[0], max_velocity=1.5, min_pressure=15, peak_factor=1.8) print(sizing.message, sizing.cost) host.document.apply("Size pipes", lambda p: apply_sizes(p, sizing)) hydrants = fire_flow_analysis(project, hydrant_candidates(project), target_lps=25)

Long calculations must not freeze the window: from flowchaos.core import workers future = workers.submit(my_long_calculation, project_copy) future.add_done_callback(lambda f: print(f.result())) Copy the project first (copy.deepcopy) when the calculation runs while the user keeps editing, and change widgets only from the main thread (use a Qt signal or QTimer.singleShot(0, ...)).

The data a project holds: nodes, links, results and settings.

flowchaos.core.project.NetworkProject Field Type Meaning name str project name crs str coordinate system, for example "EPSG:32736" nodes list of NetworkNode junctions, reservoirs and tanks links list of NetworkLink pipes, pumps and valves results dict or None the stored results (see below) settings dict everything else saved with the project analysis_sections dict analysis options, profiles, curves, controls and rules, as sections of rows Method Returns node(id), link(id) the element with that id link_length_m(link) the length used by the analysis link_path_points(link) the drawn points of a link, from start to end next_node_name(type), next_link_name(type) a free name with the project's prefixes to_dict(), NetworkProject.from_dict(data) the project as plain data and back

Field Meaning id unique id (use flowchaos.core.project.new_id() for new elements) name the name shown to users node_type "JUNCTION", "RESERVOIR" or "TANK" x, y position in the project's coordinate system elevation_m hydraulic elevation (for a reservoir: its water level) demand_lps design withdrawal attributes a dict of everything else: ground level, starting concentration, imported fields, labels Useful attribute keys: ground_elevation_m, initial_quality, fields (every column of the file the element came from), flowchaos_layer_id (its imported layer), hydrant.

Field Meaning id, name as for nodes link_type "PIPE", "PUMP" or "VALVE" start_node, end_node node ids diameter_mm internal diameter roughness in the units of the head loss formula status "OPEN", "CLOSED" or "CV" (check valve) attributes vertices (bend points), material, pressure_class, bulk_coeff, wall_coeff, size_locked, imported fields

After a run, project.results holds: { "method": "...", "nodes": [{"name": "J1", "head_m": 112.4, "pressure_m": 31.2, "demand_lps": 1.5, "quality": None}, ...], "links": [{"name": "P1", "flow_lps": 12.3, "velocity_mps": 0.81, "headloss_m": 0.42, "status": "OPEN"}, ...], "time_steps": [{"time_seconds": 0, "nodes": [...], "links": [...]}, ...], # extended period only }

project.settings keeps what is saved with the project, for example: layer_labels, layer_styles, layer_display, legends, contour_layers, layouts, metadata, project_info, elevation_source, predefined_scales. Plugins should use their own key: "plugin:<id>".
Complete plugins to copy and adapt.

A table the user can copy into a spreadsheet. from collections import defaultdict from PySide6.QtWidgets import QDialog, QTableWidget, QTableWidgetItem, QVBoxLayout def register(host): def run(): project = host.document.project lengths = defaultdict(float) for link in project.links: if link.link_type == "PIPE": lengths[link.diameter_mm] += project.link_length_m(link) dialog = QDialog(host.main_window) dialog.setWindowTitle("Pipe length by diameter") table = QTableWidget(len(lengths), 2, dialog) table.setHorizontalHeaderLabels(["Diameter (mm)", "Length (m)"]) for row, (diameter, length) in enumerate(sorted(lengths.items())): table.setItem(row, 0, QTableWidgetItem(f"{diameter:g}")) table.setItem(row, 1, QTableWidgetItem(f"{length:,.1f}")) QVBoxLayout(dialog).addWidget(table) dialog.resize(360, 400) dialog.exec() # every table can be copied with right-click or Ctrl+C host.add_plugin_action("Pipe Length by Diameter", run, "Total length of pipe for each diameter")

Runs the analysis, then selects and zooms to the junctions below a pressure. from PySide6.QtWidgets import QInputDialog from flowchaos.core.solver_backend import run_with_best_backend def register(host): def run(): limit, ok = QInputDialog.getDouble(host.main_window, "Low pressure", "Minimum pressure (m):", 15, 0, 200, 1) if not ok: return project = host.document.project results = run_with_best_backend(project) low = {r.name for r in results.nodes if r.pressure_m < limit} ids = {("node", n.id) for n in project.nodes if n.name in low and n.node_type == "JUNCTION"} host.canvas.set_selection(ids) if ids: host.canvas.zoom_to_selection() host.statusBar().showMessage(f"{len(ids)} junction(s) below {limit:g} m.", 8000) host.add_plugin_action("Select Low-Pressure Junctions", run)

section: A window of your own, with work in the background
text: import copy from PySide6.QtCore import QObject, Signal from PySide6.QtWidgets import QLabel, QPushButton, QVBoxLayout, QWidget from flowchaos.core import workers from flowchaos.core.solver_backend import run_extended_with_best_backend class _Done(QObject): finished = Signal(object) class PeakWindow(QWidget): def __init__(self, host): super().__init__() self.host = host self.setWindowTitle("Peak velocity over a day") self.label = QLabel("Press Run.") button = QPushButton("Run 24 hours") button.clicked.connect(self.run) layout = QVBoxLayout(self) layout.addWidget(self.label) layout.addWidget(button) self.done = _Done() self.done.finished.connect(self.show_result) def run(self): project = copy.deepcopy(self.host.document.project) # the user may keep editing self.label.setText("Running...") workers.submit(lambda: self.done.finished.emit(run_extended_with_best_backend(project, 86400, 3600))) def show_result(self, results): peak = max((abs(l.velocity_mps), l.name, f.time_seconds // 3600) for f in results.frames for l in f.hydraulics.links) self.label.setText(f"Highest velocity {peak[0]:.2f} m/s in {peak[1]} at hour {peak[2]}.") def register(host): host.add_plugin_action("Peak Velocity Over a Day", lambda: host.show_tool_window("peak-velocity", lambda: PeakWindow(host)))

Keep the calculation in a function and test it without a window: from flowchaos.core.examples import sample_water_network def test_total_length(): project = sample_water_network() total = sum(project.link_length_m(l) for l in project.links if l.link_type == "PIPE") assert total > 0
